proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.area_save_gate
proposed_widenings.justification: Incendiary Cloud's core mechanic is a persistent area that applies a save gate (Dex save, 10d8 fire / half on success) each time a creature enters the area, when the area moves into a creature's space, or when a creature ends its turn there. OngoingOperation only supports roll_modifier and damage_on_hit — neither covers a save-gated damage effect in an ongoing area context.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When the cloud appears, each creature in it makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d8 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature must also make this save when the Sphere moves into its space and when it enters the Sphere or ends its turn there.

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.once_per_turn_guard
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell explicitly restricts each creature to at most one save per turn across all triggers (entering, being entered upon, ending turn). This per-turn deduplication guard has no current representation in OngoingOperation or any other surface type.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature makes this save only once per turn.

proposed_widenings.name: Attachment.area with self_move_per_turn
proposed_widenings.justification: The cloud moves 10 feet in a caster-chosen direction at the start of each of the caster's turns. This is area self-movement, not creature movement (force_move/move). No current Attachment shape or operation type captures a caster-directed area displacement per turn.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The cloud moves 10 feet away from you in a direction you choose at the start of each of your turns.

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.block_sight (heavily_obscured)
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell makes its area Heavily Obscured (a rules-defined visibility state that affects attack rolls and ability checks). There is no surface-level operation type for granting/applying Heavily Obscured to an area.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The cloud's area is Heavily Obscured.

notes: No dhall/json/trace authored. The dominant gap is OngoingOperation lacking a save-gate variant; the ongoing_effect family with an area attachment is otherwise structurally correct. Area self-movement and heavy obscurement are secondary surface gaps. The one-time initial burst (when the cloud first appears) and the ongoing per-turn trigger are the same mechanic (same save, same damage) so a single area_save_gate operation with an appropriate trigger enumeration (on_enter | on_area_enters | on_turn_end) would cover both without needing a separate activation phase.
